Popup Finalists

Three ways to open a place, each a real travel object. Each starts with the busiest real place (VEGA). Pinch to zoom.

The same in all three

  • Name and your note read first. A normal note shows whole.
  • Type is the small line under the name.
  • Directions, Star, Visited: one tap each, same size. Star only filled when starred.
  • Signed out: Star and Visited greyed out. Directions still works, since it changes nothing.
  • Map pins unchanged.

1 / 3

Postcard

The postcard you write to yourself. Your note is the message, the pin’s seal is the postage stamp, the address sits on the address lines, and Visited is the postmark.

From
Postcards and the Yosemite trail scrapbook; the passport stamps for the postmark.

Why it’s here. Every part of the postcard holds real content, nothing is decoration. The address finally reads as small print. The pin’s seal becomes the stamp, so the pin and the card are one idea.

Weak spot. Visited sits up by the stamp, not with the other two buttons. The message column is narrower, so long notes wrap more. The list is away while a place is open.

2 / 3

Luggage Label

The hotel label, with the map as its picture. An orange band carries the pin’s seal as its emblem and the name in label lettering.

From
Hotel de la Poste (Cortina), Hotel Guynemer (Casablanca) and Hotel Savoy luggage labels.

Why it’s here. The cleanest busiest view of the three: name, then your note, then the buttons. The map above plays the label’s picture. The band is the only colour on screen and it means “this place is open”.

Weak spot. A big orange band. Nothing on the label changes when you’ve been there, unless you want the postmark option (last still). The list is away while a place is open.

3 / 3

Hanging Tag

A luggage tag hanging off the pin on a string. The address is on the tear-off stub. A long note: turn the tag over.

From
Luggage tags and labels; the trail scrapbook’s paper and string.

Why it’s here. The pin is the knot the tag hangs from, the most physical link between pin and card. It stays on the map, and the list drops to its header so the tag has room and the orange row is out of the way.

Weak spot. It still covers the map below the pin. The list lowers while a tag is open. Every open moves the map so the pin sits near the top.

Cut, and why

Say the word and any of these comes back.

  • Passport Stamp. The card is an entry stamp; Mark Visited inks it. Cut: an empty dashed frame on every place you haven’t been, and a box around the name inside a box. Its stamp-down motion lives on in the Postcard’s postmark.
  • Card File. The row is pulled out of the list as an index card, the note typed on ruled lines. Cut: the quietest of the five, its look is mostly rules and a borrowed typewriter font. UX liked how it handles Plans. Its pull-out motion can be how any finalist opens from the list.
  • Pinned Note. The pin as a pushpin holding a note scrap to the map. Cut before you saw it: once drawn it was the old popup tilted a degree. Not more fun.
The map is a stand-in drawing (real tiles can’t load where these were made). Rendered in Chrome, not checked on iPhone. Details: design/popup-hierarchy/round3/README.md.
